newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 3-mth current acct gap up at $1.13 bln.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 3-mth current acct gap up at $1.13 bln.

text.p: The Philippine current account deficit in the first three months of the year widened to $1.13 billion from the year-ago level of $923 million, the Central Bank reported on Wednesday.
A bigger merchandise trade deficit and the slower growth in the non-merchandise trade surplus led to the wider current account deficit, the Central Bank statement said.
As a ratio to gross national product (GNP), the current account deficit in the first quarter was 4.9 percent against 4.5 percent last year, the Central Bank said.
The Philippines projected its 1997 current account deficit to reach $4.1 billion, equivalent to 4.2 percent of the GNP.
However, capital inflows had offset the current account deficit, resulting in a balance of payments surplus of $570 million during the period, the statement said.

"We are pleased to note the balance of payments for the first quarter of this year registered an over-performance of $559 million relative to the first quarter programme of an $11 million surplus," it added.
The favourable developments in the first quarter boosted the central bank's gross international reserves to $11.95 billion at the end of March from $11.7 billion by the end of 1996.
